newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: VW,Ford recall models made in Portugal.
newsitem.headline: VW,Ford recall models made in Portugal.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen and U.S. group Ford said on Thursday they were recalling for checks passenger vans produced at a plant in Portugal and sold across Europe because of brake and door lock problems.

Volkswagen was recalling for checks 21,600 Sharan multi-purpose vehicles and Ford thousands of Galaxy models produced at the AutoEuropa joint venture at Palmela, 50 km (30 miles) south of Lisbon, company spokesmen told Reuters.
"We do not know the exact number of Galaxies affected, but we estimate it should be thousands across Europe, including 400 in Portugal," Ford spokesman Artur Lemos said.
He said the Galaxy multi-purpose vehicles were produced at the AutoEuropa plant between December 1995 and July 1996.
Volkswagen spokesman Hector De Morais said: "Volkswagen is asking clients automatically by letter to have their vehicles checked for free at their local concessionary garages."
He said Volkswagen was recalling 14,600 Sharan vehicles produced since September this year to check for possible problems with the brake pedal.
Another 7,000 would be checked for possible faults with the lubrication of door locks, he added.
Lemos said the Ford Galaxies had the same problems as the VW Sharans as both models were produced at AutoEuropa.
He said the brake problem was a faulty spring that affected the mobility of the pedal. "There is no risk during braking. It is a small problem easily fixed," he added.

The AutoEuropa joint venture between Ford and Volkswagen, the biggest foreign investment project in Portugal, now produces a total of 520 passenger vans a day, AutoEuropa spokeswoman Carmo Jardim told Reuters.
Production is divided equally between Ford and Volkswagen and includes a relatively small number of Seat Alhambra passenger vans, she said.
It was not immediately known whether the Alhambras, which were all produced for export, would also be recalled for checks, Seat spokeswoman Teresa Lameiras said.
The AutoEuropa plant, which was officially inaugurated in April 1995, employs about 4,000 people and contributes around 2.7 percent of Portugal's total economic output and 11 percent of its exports.
